text: Problem set 2 Problem 1. Let V be a vector space over a field F . Prove the following statements. (i) Let u, v ∈ V be distinct vectors in V . Then u, v is linearly dependent if and only if u or v is a multiple of each other. (ii) Any subset of linearly independent vectors is linearly independent. (iii) Any set containing a set of linearly dependent vectors is linearly dependent. In particular, if a set of vectors contain a zero vector then it is linearly dependent. (iv) Let v1, . . . , vn be linearly independent. Suppose v1 + w, v2 + w, · · · , vn + w are linearly dependent, then w ∈ span(v1, . . . , vn). (v) Let v1, v2, v3, v4 be some vectors in V . Show that span(v1, v2, v3, v4) = span(v1 − v2, v2 − v3, v3 − v4, v4) by showing that any linear combination of v1, v2, v3, v4 is a linear combination of v1 − v2, v2 − v3, v3 − v4, v4 and vice versa. Problem 2. (i) Show that cos x, sin x is linearly independent in the vector space C(R). (ii) Show that ex, e2x is linearly independent in the vector space C(R). Problem 3. Define Qn(1) = {f ∈ Pn(R) : f (1) = 0}. (i) Show that Qn(1) is a subspace of Pn(R). (ii) Determine the dimension of that subspace and give a basis. (iii) Show that Pn(R) = Qn(1) + span(1) where 1 is the polynomial 0xn + 0xn−1 + · · · + 0x + 1. Problem 4. Let V be a vector space over a field F and V1, V2 ⊂ V be subspaces of V . (i) If there exist v1 ∈ V1 and v2 ∈ V2 such that v1 /∈ V2 and v2 /∈ V1. Show that v1 + v2 /∈ V1 ∪ V2. (ii) Show that V1 ∪ V2 is a subspace of V if and only if V1 ⊂ V2 or V2 ⊂ V1. Remark 5. This problem should be compared with Proposition 2.26 in Lecture 2, showing that the smallest vector space containing V1 ∪ V2 is V1 + V2. 1
